- entire: Drive the Entire CLI (entire) for checkpoints, agent sessions, code provenance, and multi-agent review. Use when the user mentions Entire, checkpoints, session tracking, "entire why/blame/experts", agent activity recaps, or when a repo contains .entire/ and you need to inspect or manage tracked agent work.
- aside: Answer a quick side question without interrupting or losing context from the current task. Resume work automatically after answering.
- build-fix: Detect the project build system and incrementally fix build/type errors with minimal safe changes.
- checkpoint: Create, verify, or list workflow checkpoints after running verification checks.
- code-review: Code review — local uncommitted changes or GitHub PR (pass PR number/URL for PR mode)
- cost-report: Generate a local Claude Code cost report from a cost-tracker SQLite database.
- cpp-build: Fix C++ build errors, CMake issues, and linker problems incrementally. Invokes the cpp-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- cpp-review: Comprehensive C++ code review for memory safety, modern C++ idioms, concurrency, and security. Invokes the cpp-reviewer agent.
- cpp-test: Enforce TDD workflow for C++. Write GoogleTest tests first, then implement. Verify coverage with gcov/lcov.
- ecc-guide: Navigate ECC's current agents, skills, commands, hooks, install profiles, and docs from the live repository surface.
- evolve: Analyze instincts and suggest or generate evolved structures
- fastapi-review: Review a FastAPI application for architecture, async correctness, dependency injection, Pydantic schemas, security, performance, and testability.
- feature-dev: Guided feature development with codebase understanding and architecture focus
- flutter-build: Fix Dart analyzer errors and Flutter build failures incrementally. Invokes the dart-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- flutter-review: Review Flutter/Dart code for idiomatic patterns, widget best practices, state management, performance, accessibility, and security. Invokes the flutter-reviewer agent.
- flutter-test: Run Flutter/Dart tests, report failures, and incrementally fix test issues. Covers unit, widget, golden, and integration tests.
- gan-build: Run a generator/evaluator build loop for implementation tasks with bounded iterations and scoring.
- gan-design: Run a generator/evaluator design loop for frontend or visual work with bounded iterations and scoring.
- go-build: Fix Go build errors, go vet warnings, and linter issues incrementally. Invokes the go-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- go-review: Comprehensive Go code review for idiomatic patterns, concurrency safety, error handling, and security. Invokes the go-reviewer agent.
- go-test: Enforce TDD workflow for Go. Write table-driven tests first, then implement. Verify 80%+ coverage with go test -cover.
- gradle-build: Fix Gradle build errors for Android and KMP projects
- harness-audit: Run a deterministic repository harness audit and return a prioritized scorecard.
- hookify: Create hooks to prevent unwanted behaviors from conversation analysis or explicit instructions
- hookify-configure: Enable or disable hookify rules interactively
- hookify-help: Get help with the hookify system
- hookify-list: List all configured hookify rules
- instinct-export: Export instincts from project/global scope to a file
- instinct-import: Import instincts from file or URL into project/global scope
- instinct-status: Show learned instincts (project + global) with confidence
- jira: Retrieve a Jira ticket, analyze requirements, update status, or add comments. Uses the jira-integration skill and MCP or REST API.
- kotlin-build: Fix Kotlin/Gradle build errors, compiler warnings, and dependency issues incrementally. Invokes the kotlin-build-resolver agent for minimal, surgical fixes.
- kotlin-review: Comprehensive Kotlin code review for idiomatic patterns, null safety, coroutine safety, and security. Invokes the kotlin-reviewer agent.
- kotlin-test: Enforce TDD workflow for Kotlin. Write Kotest tests first, then implement. Verify 80%+ coverage with Kover.
- learn: Extract reusable patterns from the current session and save them as candidate skills or guidance.
- learn-eval: Extract reusable patterns from the session, self-evaluate quality before saving, and determine the right save location (Global vs Project).
- loop-start: Start a managed autonomous loop pattern with safety defaults and explicit stop conditions.
- loop-status: Inspect active loop state, progress, failure signals, and recommended intervention.
- model-route: Recommend the best model tier for the current task based on complexity, risk, and budget.
- multi-backend: Run a backend-focused multi-model workflow for APIs, algorithms, data, and business logic.

- multi-frontend: Run a frontend-focused multi-model workflow for components, layouts, animation, and UI polish.

- multi-workflow: Run a full multi-model development workflow with research, planning, execution, optimization, and review.

- projects: List known projects and their instinct statistics

- skill-create: Analyze local git history to extract coding patterns and generate SKILL.md files. Local version of the Skill Creator GitHub App.

- claude-powerline:powerline: Claude Powerline statusline setup wizard
- entire:address-findings: Address the review findings posted on an Entire trail: fetch the trail's open findings, fix the code, and resolve them on the trail. Use when the user gives a trail URL or number and asks to address, fix, or resolve its findings or review comments. Not for local diff review — that is the `review` skill.
- entire:explain: Explains the intent behind source code by finding original session transcripts. Use explain with a function, file, or line of code to understand why it exists.
- entire:recall: Use when the user describes a task and wants to know whether something similar has been done before, then turn the closest prior session into a task playbook. Triggers on phrases like "have we done this before", "recall how we did X", "find similar work", "any precedent for", "has anyone solved", "is there a template for", and "how did we do this last time"
- entire:replay: Use when the user wants to step through a feature's checkpoints chronologically, pausing at each step to ask questions. Triggers on phrases like "replay <feature>", "walk me through how X was built", "show me the journey of", "step me through how Y was implemented", and "replay the last week"
- entire:review: Review code changes on the current branch using checkpoint transcript context to understand developer intent before auditing the diff. Use when the user asks for a code review, wants to review branch changes, or asks to audit recent work before merging.
- entire:search: Use when the user wants to find prior work, checkpoints, or agent conversations by topic, repo, branch, author, or recent time window, or to search code content across repositories
- entire:session-crosslink: Use when an agent session ran outside the repo whose commits should record it — e.g. launched from a higher-level folder, a non-Entire repo, or one repo but editing another — to attach the session to each affected Entire-enabled repo's HEAD commit.
- entire:session-handoff: Use when the user wants to continue work from one agent in another agent, inspect recent sessions, or summarize a saved session or checkpoint for handoff
- entire:session-to-skill: Use when the user wants to turn one or more Entire-tracked sessions, checkpoints, or repeated agent workflows into a reusable agent skill.
- entire:teach: Use when a developer wants a topic-focused guided lesson built from canonical checkpoints, not a whole-repo overview. Triggers on phrases like "teach me <topic>", "teach me how this repo handles", "how does <topic> work in this repo", "give me a lesson on", "school me on", and "I need to learn about"
- entire:using-entire: Use for any codebase exploration or understanding task — reads historical intent from Entire checkpoints instead of guessing. Orchestrates other Entire skills to give the agent provenance-backed answers about code.
- entire:what-happened: Explain why code looks the way it does by tracing the latest change for a file range or pasted snippet through `git blame` and deduplicated `entire explain` lookups. Use when the user asks what happened, says "tell me why" about a code block, is confused about a section of code, asks "wtf is going on", "why is this like this", "why was this changed", or wants provenance for a specific file block.
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- artifact-design: Design guidance and fundamentals for Artifacts.
- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, keeping state shared across viewers, or updating and republishing itself.   everywhere. It is a net *reduction* in argument count — `GetTrivyCommand` had
  eight positional parameters, which is why nobody threaded a ninth through.
- `scan.trivy_source` / `scan.gitleaks_source` take `auto | binary | image`, and
  default to `auto`, which is the historical resolution exactly — an existing
  config cannot change meaning on upgrade.
- **`binary` does not fall back to Docker.** That silent fallback is what kept
  D27 invisible: a path that was never read still produced working scans, run by
  something other than what was asked for.

All three invariants confirmed to bite: ignoring the configured path,
reinstating the Docker fallback, and hard-coding the tool name in the builder
each fail their own test.
**The scan caches ignored the configuration context. Fixed** by
`internal/cache/scan_file.go`, found while planning the configuration view.

`config.yaml` is per context — `LoadContext` reads `config-<name>.yaml` — but
all six caches lived flat under `~/.devdesk/cache/`, and `browser-selection.json`
was the only one with a context dimension. `workspaces_dir` and the registry
list being per context, two contexts legitimately hold different roots and
different images in one namespace.

Nothing showed it, because the caches were only ever *queried*: you ask about
the image in front of you, and the answer is right whoever wrote it. The
inventory view planned for §2 of the configuration-view plan *lists* everything
the cache holds, which is what would have put another context's findings on
screen. So this is a latent inaccuracy fixed before the change that would have
exposed it, not a defect anyone reported.

`ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` are now bound to a context at
construction; their method signatures are unchanged. The legacy flat file is
recognised by `Contexts == nil` after unmarshalling into the versioned struct —
no field matches — and is **upgraded on the first open rather than at the next
write**. Deferring it would let each context that opened the file claim the
legacy entries in turn, making ownership depend on write order;
`TestAFlatImageCacheMigratesIntoTheOpeningContext` is what pins that, and it
fails when the write-back is removed.

`config.CurrentContextName()` came out of it, collapsing the

already each carried a copy of.

1	# A configuration view, and `security` becomes an inventory
2	
3	Status: planned, not started. Decisions below are settled; open questions are
4	marked as such and are the only things left to arbitrate.
5	
6	## What was decided
7	
8	| Question | Answer |
9	|---|---|
10	| Scope of the config view | **Scalars only.** The ~29 simple fields. Lists — monitors, registries — stay where they are consulted. |
11	| Fate of `security` | **Inventory of what has been scanned.** `:sec` opens a unified images + workspaces table read from the two caches. |
12	| Free-target picker (`b`) | **Removed.** What gets scanned is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`. |
13	| Scope of a configuration | **Per context.** One config per context, as today; the view edits the current one and must name it. |
14	| Reaching a result from its row | **Preserved.** `enter` on a scanned image or repository opens the findings, `esc` returns to that row. |
15	| `secret_backend` changed at runtime | **Re-resolve, confirm first, migrate nothing.** See below. |
16	
17	## The fact this plan rests on
18	
19	The flow being proposed is already 80 % built, and nobody noticed because the
20	form kept standing in front of it.
21

# A configuration view, and `security` becomes an inventory

Status: planned, not started. Decisions below are settled; open questions are
marked as such and are the only things left to arbitrate.

## What was decided

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Scope of the config view | **Scalars only.** The ~29 simple fields. Lists — monitors, registries — stay where they are consulted. |
| Fate of `security` | **Inventory of what has been scanned.** `:sec` opens a unified images + workspaces table read from the two caches. |
| Free-target picker (`b`) | **Removed.** What gets scanned is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`. |
| Scope of a configuration | **Per context.** One config per context, as today; the view edits the current one and must name it. |
| Reaching a result from its row | **Preserved.** `enter` on a scanned image or repository opens the findings, `esc` returns to that row. |
| `secret_backend` changed at runtime | **Re-resolve, confirm first, migrate nothing.** See below. |

## The fact this plan rests on

The flow being proposed is already 80 % built, and nobody noticed because the
form kept standing in front of it.

```go
// internal/ui/workspaces/actions.go:143
func (m Model) getScanOptions() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }

// internal/ui/oci_resources/images.go:79
func (m Model) defaultScanOpts() scan.ScanOptions { … m.config.Scan.EnableVuln … }
```

Byte-for-byte identical, both reading the config. `ctrl+s` on an image or on a
repository has not gone through the security form for some time. And
`NewWithPreloadedResult` already opens straight on `StateResults`.

So this is not a redesign. It is deleting the one remaining path that reads
something *other* than the config, and giving `:sec` a landing page that is not
an empty form.

---

## Phase 0 — D26: `IgnoreEOL` is dropped on two of the three scan paths

`oci_resources` and `workspaces` keep running their own scans — they are the
primary trigger points by design. It is the cross-view round trip that goes.

### `OriginView` stays — it carries navigation, not options

An earlier draft of this plan listed `OriginView` as removable. That was wrong,
and it is the mechanism behind a hard requirement: **a scan launched from a row
must be readable from that same row when it finishes.**

The round trip already works and is not touched by any phase:

```

                       → openSecurityView(NewWithPreloadedResult, origin)
```

stays is the record of where `esc` returns to — and it gets more use, not less,
since the inventory becomes a third origin.

**One consequence to handle.** `handleWorkspaceScanResultLoaded` currently falls

of hitting a dead end. With no form, that fallback re-triggers the scan in the

### The scan caches must become per-context

dimension (`map[string][]string`, context → entries).

Today this is invisible because the caches are only ever *queried* — you ask
about the image in front of you. **Phase 2 makes it visible**: the inventory

`workspaces_dir` being per context makes it concrete: two contexts legitimately
point at different roots and land in one namespace.

  shaped exactly like `browser_selection.go`.
- Existing flat entries migrate into whichever context is current on first load.

`shared.State.Tools []ToolInfo` and shows exactly this. It is not duplicated on

Only once phases 1 and 2 are merged.

| Goes | Size |
|---|---|
| `internal/ui/security/form.go` | 271 lines |
| `renderInputView`, `formLeftColumn`, `formRightColumn`, `renderCheckbox`, `renderTargetTypeField`, `renderTargetPathField`, `renderStartButton`, `renderAdvancedTextInput` | ~120 lines |

| `SelectionRequestMsg` / `SelectionResultMsg` / `SelectionCancelledMsg` and the browser bridge | — |

1. `applyServerModeConstraints` — a Trivy server URL forces `misconfig`,

|---|---|---|
| 0 — `IgnoreEOL` (D26) | yes | — |

| 0c — tool source and paths (D27) | yes | — |

and each is worth doing whatever happens to the config view. 0b fixes a latent
inaccuracy that phase 2 would otherwise put on screen; 0c is what makes the

103		s.Spinner = spinner.Dot
104		s.Style = theme.SpinnerStyle()
105	
106		ti := textinput.New()
107		ti.Placeholder = "/path/to/scan"
108		ti.CharLimit = 256
109		ti.Width = 50
110		theme.StyleTextInput(&ti)
111	
112		t := datatable.New(datatable.Config[scan.Finding]{
113			Columns:        findingColumns(),
114			SortColumn:     -1, // the order the scanner reported
115			SelectedStyles: findingSelectedStyles,
116		})
117	
118		// Advanced options textinputs
119		trivyServer := textinput.New()
120		trivyServer.Placeholder = "https://trivy-server:4954"
121		trivyServer.CharLimit = 256
122		trivyServer.Width = 40
123		theme.StyleTextInput(&trivyServer)
124		if cfg.Scan.TrivyServer != "" {
125			trivyServer.SetValue(cfg.Scan.TrivyServer)
126		}
127	
128		gitleaksConfig := textinput.New()
129		gitleaksConfig.Placeholder = "/path/to/.gitleaks.toml"
130		gitleaksConfig.CharLimit = 256
131		gitleaksConfig.Width = 40
132		theme.StyleTextInput(&gitleaksConfig)
133	
134		return Model{
135			config:              cfg,
136			state:               StateInput,
137			targetType:          "directory",
138			enableVuln:          cfg.Scan.EnableVuln,
139			enableSecret:        cfg.Scan.EnableSecret,
140			enableMisconfig:     cfg.Scan.EnableMisconfig,
141			enableLicense:       cfg.Scan.EnableLicense,
142			generateSBOM:        cfg.Scan.GenerateSBOM,
143			ignoreUnfixed:       cfg.Scan.IgnoreUnfixed,
144			ignoreEOL:           cfg.Scan.IgnoreEOL,
145			gitleaksHistory:     cfg.Scan.GitleaksHistory,
146			targetInput:         ti,
147			spinner:             s,
148			findingsTable:       t,
149			focusedField:        0,
150			severityFilter:      "all",
151			trivyServerInput:    trivyServer,
152			gitleaksConfigInput: gitleaksConfig,
153		}
154	}
155	
156	// NewWithTarget creates a security view pre-populated with a target path
157	func NewWithTarget(cfg *config.Config, target string) Model {
158		m := New(cfg)
159		m.prefilledTarget = target
160		m.targetPath = target
161		m.targetInput.SetValue(target)
162		return m
163	}
164	
165	// NewWithImageTarget creates a security view pre-populated with an image target.
166	// Set returnToOCI=true when opened from the OCI images view: launching the scan will send
167	// the configured options back to OCI images view instead of running the scan in-place.
168	func NewWithImageTarget(cfg *config.Config, imageName string, returnToOCI bool) Model {
169		m := New(cfg)
170		m.prefilledTarget = imageName
171		m.targetPath = imageName
172		m.targetType = "image"
173		m.isImageScan = true
174		m.returnToOCIImages = returnToOCI
175		if imageName == "all" {
176			m.targetInput.SetValue("all")
177			m.targetInput.Placeholder = "All OCI Images"
178		} else {
179			m.targetInput.SetValue(imageName)
180		}
181		return m
182	}
183	
184	// NewWithTargetReturnToWorkspaces creates a security view pre-populated with a target path.
185	// After the scan completes, results are sent back to the workspaces view.
186	func NewWithTargetReturnToWorkspaces(cfg *config.Config, target string) Model {
187		m := NewWithTarget(cfg, target)
188		m.returnToWorkspaces = true
189		return m
190	}
191	
192	// NewWithPreloadedResult creates a security view in StateDetails with a pre-loaded scan result.
193	// Used to display cached workspace scan results without re-scanning.
194	func NewWithPreloadedResult(cfg *config.Config, result *scan.Result) Model {
195		m := New(cfg)
196		m.state = StateResults
197		m.result = result
198		m.targetPath = result.Target
199		m.activeTab = TabCVE
200		m.severityFilter = "all"
201		// Filled here rather than waiting for the first WindowSizeMsg: the rows do
202		// not depend on the width any more, so nothing was gained by deferring and
203		// the table was empty until the terminal happened to report its size.
204		m.updateFindingsTable()
205		return m
206	}
207	
208	// Init initializes the model
209	func (m Model) Init() tea.Cmd {
210		return tea.Batch(
211			m.checkDependencies(),
212			m.spinner.Tick,
213		)
214	}
215	
216	// checkDependencies verifies tool availability
217	func (m Model) checkDependencies() tea.Cmd {
218		// Copied out of the model before the Cmd runs: a Cmd must not read state
219		// Update() may be writing (Rule 110).
220		scanCfg := m.config.Scan
221		return func() tea.Msg {
222			return DepsCheckedMsg{Deps: scan.CheckDependencies(scanCfg)}
223		}
224	}
225	
226	// InEditMode reports whether a field or a modal has the keyboard, which is what
227	// stops the router claiming ":", "q" and "?" for itself.
228	//
229	// The scanning, results and details states used to be listed here too, for one
230	// reason: it was the only way to be handed esc. The router forwards esc
231	// unconditionally now (§1.3 D15), so those states are ordinary again — and get
232	// the command line, the help overlay and quit back with them.
233	func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
234		isTextInput := m.state == StateInput && (m.focusedField == 1 || m.focusedField == 7 || m.focusedField == 10)
235		return isTextInput || m.confirmModal != nil
236	}

1	package security
2	
3	import (
4		"fmt"
5		"log"
6	
7		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/spinner"
8		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
9	
10		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/scan"
11		sharedcomponents "github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
12	)
13	
14	// Update handles messages
15	func (m Model) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
16		// Handle confirm modal messages first (before passing to modal)
17		switch msg := msg.(type) {
18		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalYesMsg:
19			// User confirmed to ignore the secret
20			if m.findingToIgnore != nil {
21				finding := *m.findingToIgnore
22				targetDir := m.targetPath
23				m.confirmModal = nil
24				m.findingToIgnore = nil
25				return m, func() tea.Msg {
26					err := scan.AddToGitleaksIgnore(targetDir, finding)
27					return SecretIgnoredMsg{Finding: finding, Error: err}
28				}
29			}
30			m.confirmModal = nil
31			m.findingToIgnore = nil
32			return m, nil
33	
34		case sharedcomponents.ConfirmModalNoMsg:
35			// User cancelled
36			m.confirmModal = nil
37			m.findingToIgnore = nil
38			return m, nil
39	
40		case tea.WindowSizeMsg:
41			m.width = msg.Width
42			m.height = msg.Height
43			// Widths and height in one call; SetHeight accounts for the header row
44			// internally, so m.height goes through as it is. Rows no longer depend
45			// on the width — bubbles truncates each cell to its own column — so
46			// there is nothing to rebuild here.
47			m.findingsTable.Resize(m.width, max(m.height, 5))
48			// Update details viewport size and refresh content
49			m.detailsViewport.Width = msg.Width
50			m.detailsViewport.Height = msg.Height
51			if m.state == StateDetails {
52				m.detailsViewport.SetContent(m.buildDetailsContent())
53			}
54			return m, nil
55	
56		case tea.KeyMsg:
57			// Pass key messages to confirm modal if active
58			if m.confirmModal != nil {
59				var cmd tea.Cmd
60				m.confirmModal, cmd = m.confirmModal.Update(msg)
61				return m, cmd
62			}
63			return m.handleKeyMsg(msg)
64	
65		case DepsCheckedMsg:
66			m.deps = msg.Deps
67			return m, nil
68	
69		case ScanCompleteMsg:
70			return m.handleScanComplete(msg)
71	
72		case SecretIgnoredMsg:
73			if msg.Error != nil {
74				log.Printf("ERROR [security] ignore secret %s: %v", msg.Finding.File, msg.Error)
75				m.statusMessage = "Failed to ignore secret — check logs"
76			} else {
77				m.statusMessage = fmt.Sprintf("Added %s to .gitleaksignore", msg.Finding.File)
78			}
79			return m, clearStatusCmd()
80	
81		case clearStatusMsg:
82			m.statusMessage = ""
83			return m, nil
84	
85		case SelectionResultMsg:
86			m.targetPath = msg.Path
87			m.targetInput.SetValue(msg.Path)
88			return m, nil
89	
90		case SelectionCancelledMsg:
91			return m, nil
92	
93		case StartScanMsg:
94			return m.startScan()
95	
96		case ScanProgressMsg:
97			return m.handleScanProgress(msg)
98	
99		case spinner.TickMsg:
100			if m.state == StateScanning {
101				var cmd tea.Cmd
102				m.spinner, cmd = m.spinner.Update(msg)
103				return m, cmd
104			}
105		}
106	
107		return m, nil
108	}
109	
110	// handleKeyMsg processes keyboard input
111	func (m Model) handleKeyMsg(msg tea.KeyMsg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
112		switch m.state {
113		case StateInput:
114			return m.handleInputState(msg)
115		case StateScanning:
116			if msg.String() == "esc" || msg.String() == "ctrl+c" {
117				return m.cancelCurrentScan()
118			}
119			return m, nil
120		case StateResults:
121			return m.handleResultsState(msg)
122		case StateDetails:
123			return m.handleDetailsState(msg)
124		}
125		return m, nil
126	}

1	// Package datatable is the shared mechanism behind the application's tables.
2	//
3	// What was shared before was only the *look* — theme.DefaultTableStyles,
4	// TableStylesForState/ForSeverity, components.FilterBar, theme.TimeAgo. Column
5	// widths, sorting, sort arrows, filter matching, cursor clamping and
6	// cursor-to-object resolution were written out again in each of the fifteen
7	// tables, and drifted:
8	//
9	//   - Rule 116's width invariant is broken by five of the twelve copies, which
10	//     clamp per column after the remainder has been computed (see widths.go).
11	//   - Two of eight clamp the cursor when the row count shrinks; the rest leave
12	//     it dangling, and oci_resources compensates by jumping to the top on every
13	//     filter toggle, throwing away the scroll position.
14	//   - Nine getSelectedX() replay filter-then-sort by hand to map a cursor back
15	//     to an object, with nothing tying that ordering to the one the rows were
16	//     built from. If they drift, the action lands on the wrong object and says
17	//     nothing. That is the duplication worth removing on correctness grounds.
18	//
19	// Here the filtered, sorted slice is built once and kept, so Selected() cannot
20	// disagree with what is on screen, and Cell func(T) string gives styled text
21	// nowhere to go — Rule 122 by construction rather than by review.
22	package datatable
23	
24	import (
25		"slices"
26		"sort"
27		"strings"
28	
29		"github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles/table"
30		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
31	
32		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/components"
33		"github.com/anthnel/devdesk/internal/ui/theme"
34	)
35	
36	// Column describes one column and how to get its value out of an item.
37	type Column[T any] struct {
38		Title string
39		// MinWidth is what the column asks for. It is a request, not a guarantee:
40		// when the terminal is too narrow for every request, the shortfall is
41		// shared out rather than each column defending its own floor.
42		MinWidth int
43		// Flex is the column's share of the space left over. 0 keeps it at
44		// MinWidth; the leftover is split between the flexible ones by weight.
45		Flex int
46		// Cell returns the text for this column. Plain text only: bubbles/table
47		// truncates with runewidth, which does not understand ANSI, so a styled
48		// string is cut mid-escape and bleeds over every row below it (Rule 122).
49		// Taking a string rather than a styled value is what makes that
50		// unexpressible here.
51		Cell func(T) string
52		// Less sorts by this column. Nil means the column cannot be sorted by, and
53		// `.` skips it.
54		Less func(a, b T) bool
55		// Search is what the text filter matches against. Nil means the column does
56		// not participate.
57		Search func(T) string
58	}
59	
60	// Config is everything a view has to say about its table.
61	type Config[T any] struct {
62		Columns []Column[T]
63		// Tokens are the toggle filters shown in the bar (Rule 136).
64		Tokens []components.FilterToken
65		// TokenMatch decides whether an item passes the active toggles. Nil means
66		// the toggles are ignored, which is only sensible with no Tokens.
67		TokenMatch func(item T, active map[string]bool) bool
68		// SortColumn is the column sorted by on open; -1 for no initial sort.
69		SortColumn int
70		// SelectedStyles returns the table styles to use while the given item is
71		// under the cursor — that is the only thing bubbles/table can vary per
72		// selection, and it is what containers and security each re-derived by
73		// hand. Returning a style rather than a state keyword is what keeps this
74		// package from having to know what a severity is. Nil means the default.
75		SelectedStyles func(T) table.Styles
76	}
77	
78	// Model is a table over a slice of T.
79	type Model[T any] struct {
80		cfg   Config[T]
81		table table.Model
82		bar   components.FilterBar
83	
84		items []T
85		// visible is the filtered, sorted slice the rows were built from. Selected()
86		// reads it rather than recomputing, so the cursor cannot point at one
87		// ordering while the screen shows another.
88		visible []T
89	
90		sortColumn int
91		sortDesc   bool
92		width      int
93	}
94	
95	// New builds a table from its configuration.
96	func New[T any](cfg Config[T]) Model[T] {
97		cols := make([]table.Column, len(cfg.Columns))
98		for i, c := range cfg.Columns {
99			cols[i] = table.Column{Title: c.Title, Width: c.MinWidth}
100		}
101		t := table.New(table.WithColumns(cols), table.WithFocused(true), table.WithHeight(10))
102		t.SetStyles(theme.DefaultTableStyles())
103	
104		bar := components.NewFilterBar()
105		if len(cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
106			bar = components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(cfg.Tokens)
107		}
108	
109		m := Model[T]{cfg: cfg, table: t, bar: bar, sortColumn: cfg.SortColumn}
110		// The invariant the rest of the file rests on: sortColumn is either -1 or a
111		// column that can actually be sorted by. Settling it once here is what lets
112		// CycleSort and sorted() stop re-checking — and what stops `.` getting stuck
113		// flipping the direction of a column with no comparator.
114		if m.sortColumn >= len(cfg.Columns) || (m.sortColumn >= 0 && cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less == nil) {
115			m.sortColumn = -1
116		}
117		return m
118	}
119	
120	// SetItems replaces the contents. Filtering, sorting, row building and the
121	// cursor clamp all happen here and only here, which is what stops a cursor from
122	// being left pointing past the end — bubbles/table's SetRows does not clamp, and
123	// the stale cursor is invisible until the user presses a key.
124	func (m *Model[T]) SetItems(items []T) {
125		m.items = items
126		m.rebuild()
127	}
128	
129	// Items returns everything held, filtered or not.
130	func (m *Model[T]) Items() []T { return m.items }
131	
132	// Visible returns what is on screen, in the order it is on screen.
133	func (m *Model[T]) Visible() []T { return m.visible }
134	
135	// Selected returns the item under the cursor. The bool is false when there is
136	// nothing to select, which is the only case a caller has to handle.
137	func (m *Model[T]) Selected() (T, bool) {
138		cursor := m.table.Cursor()
139		if cursor < 0 || cursor >= len(m.visible) {
140			var zero T
141			return zero, false
142		}
143		return m.visible[cursor], true
144	}
145	
146	// Cursor returns the selected row index.
147	func (m *Model[T]) Cursor() int { return m.table.Cursor() }
148	
149	// SetCursor puts the cursor on a row, clamped to what exists. Views that
150	// remember a position across a reload — workspaces restores one per directory
151	// level on the way back up — call this; nothing else should need it.
152	func (m *Model[T]) SetCursor(i int) {
153		if len(m.visible) == 0 {
154			return
155		}
156		m.table.SetCursor(min(max(i, 0), len(m.visible)-1))
157		m.applyStyles()
158	}
159	
160	// GotoTop moves the cursor to the first row. Views that want the cursor reset
161	// on a change of scope — security resets it when the tab changes — call this
162	// explicitly, because SetItems deliberately does not.
163	func (m *Model[T]) GotoTop() { m.table.GotoTop() }
164	
165	// FilterBar exposes the bar for RenderFooter and GetFooterHeight (Rule 136).
166	func (m *Model[T]) FilterBar() *components.FilterBar { return &m.bar }
167	
168	// InEditMode reports whether the search field has the keyboard.
169	func (m *Model[T]) InEditMode() bool { return m.bar.InEditMode() }
170	
171	// Searchable reports whether anything can be filtered: a searchable column or a
172	// toggle token. Views use it to decide whether to advertise `/` (Rule 130).
173	func (m *Model[T]) Searchable() bool {
174		if len(m.cfg.Tokens) > 0 {
175			return true
176		}
177		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
178			if c.Search != nil {
179				return true
180			}
181		}
182		return false
183	}
184	
185	// Table exposes the underlying table for rendering.
186	func (m *Model[T]) Table() *table.Model { return &m.table }
187	
188	// View renders the table.
189	func (m *Model[T]) View() string { return m.table.View() }
190	
191	// SetHeight sets the number of rows shown.
192	func (m *Model[T]) SetHeight(h int) { m.table.SetHeight(max(h, 1)) }
193	
194	// Focus and Blur move the keyboard between two tables sharing a viewport, which
195	// is what the status view does with its monitors and its certificates.
196	func (m *Model[T]) Focus() {
197		m.table.Focus()
198		m.applyStyles()
199	}
200	
201	func (m *Model[T]) Blur() {
202		m.table.Blur()
203		m.table.SetStyles(theme.BlurredTableStyles())
204	}
205	
206	// Resize recomputes the column widths for a viewport of this width (Rule 116).
207	// The width passed is the full viewport width, borders included; the borders and
208	// the per-cell padding are subtracted here so no caller has to remember to.
209	func (m *Model[T]) Resize(width, height int) {
210		m.width = width
211		widths := solveWidths(m.cfg.Columns, availableFor(width, len(m.cfg.Columns)))
212	
213		cols := m.table.Columns()
214		for i := range cols {
215			cols[i].Width = widths[i]
216			cols[i].Title = m.titleFor(i)
217		}
218		m.table.SetColumns(cols)
219		m.bar.Resize(width)
220		if height > 0 {
221			m.SetHeight(height)
222		}
223		m.applyStyles() // the selected row is pinned to this width
224	}
225	
226	// titleFor returns a column's header, with a sort arrow on the active one.
227	func (m *Model[T]) titleFor(i int) string {
228		if i != m.sortColumn {
229			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title
230		}
231		if m.sortDesc {
232			return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▼"
233		}
234		return m.cfg.Columns[i].Title + " ▲"
235	}
236	
237	// CycleSort advances the sort: ascending, descending, then on to the next
238	// sortable column (Rule 111's `.`). Returns to no sort after the last one when
239	// the table opened unsorted, so the original order stays reachable.
240	func (m *Model[T]) CycleSort() {
241		sortable := m.sortableColumns()
242		if len(sortable) == 0 {
243			return
244		}
245		switch {
246		case m.sortColumn < 0:
247			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = sortable[0], false
248		case !m.sortDesc:
249			m.sortDesc = true
250		default:
251			m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc = m.nextSortable(sortable), false
252		}
253		m.rebuild()
254		m.Resize(m.width, 0) // the arrow moved
255	}
256	
257	// nextSortable returns the column after the current one, wrapping to the first —
258	// or to -1 when the table opened unsorted, so "no sort" is a stop on the cycle.
259	//
260	// slices.Index rather than a loop with a trailing fallback: the current column
261	// is always in sortable (New guarantees it), and a fallback that cannot run is
262	// a branch nothing can ever check.
263	func (m *Model[T]) nextSortable(sortable []int) int {
264		if at := slices.Index(sortable, m.sortColumn); at+1 < len(sortable) {
265			return sortable[at+1]
266		}
267		if m.cfg.SortColumn < 0 {
268			return -1
269		}
270		return sortable[0]
271	}
272	
273	func (m *Model[T]) sortableColumns() []int {
274		var out []int
275		for i, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
276			if c.Less != nil {
277				out = append(out, i)
278			}
279		}
280		return out
281	}
282	
283	// SortState reports the column sorted by and its direction, for tests and for
284	// views that show it elsewhere. Column is -1 when nothing is sorted.
285	func (m *Model[T]) SortState() (column int, desc bool) { return m.sortColumn, m.sortDesc }
286	
287	// Update handles the keys every table shares: navigation, `/` for the search,
288	// `.` for the sort, and whatever the filter bar takes while it is focused.
289	// Anything else is left alone, so the view keeps its own actions.
290	func (m *Model[T]) Update(msg tea.Msg) tea.Cmd {
291		if m.bar.InEditMode() {
292			var cmd tea.Cmd
293			m.bar, cmd = m.bar.Update(msg)
294			m.rebuild()
295			return cmd
296		}
297	
298		key, ok := msg.(tea.KeyMsg)
299		if !ok {
300			return nil
301		}
302		switch key.String() {
303		case "/":
304			// A table with nothing to search does not claim the key: activating a
305			// search that can only ever match nothing would empty the list, and the
306			// bar the user needs to see why is not in that view's footer.
307			if !m.Searchable() {
308				return nil
309			}
310			return m.bar.ActivateSearch()
311		case ".":
312			m.CycleSort()
313		case "up", "k":
314			m.table.MoveUp(1)
315			m.applyStyles()
316		case "down", "j":
317			m.table.MoveDown(1)
318			m.applyStyles()
319		case "pgup":
320			m.table.MoveUp(m.table.Height())
321			m.applyStyles()
322		case "pgdown":
323			m.table.MoveDown(m.table.Height())
324			m.applyStyles()
325		case "g", "home":
326			m.table.GotoTop()
327			m.applyStyles()
328		case "G", "end":
329			m.table.GotoBottom()
330			m.applyStyles()
331		}
332		return nil
333	}
334	
335	// SetTokenActive toggles one of the bar's filter tokens and re-applies it.
336	func (m *Model[T]) SetTokenActive(label string, active bool) {
337		m.bar.SetTokenActive(label, active)
338		m.rebuild()
339	}
340	
341	// IsTokenActive reports whether a toggle filter is on.
342	func (m *Model[T]) IsTokenActive(label string) bool { return m.bar.IsTokenActive(label) }
343	
344	// rebuild filters, sorts, writes the rows and puts the cursor somewhere real.
345	func (m *Model[T]) rebuild() {
346		m.visible = m.sorted(m.filtered())
347	
348		rows := make([]table.Row, len(m.visible))
349		for i, item := range m.visible {
350			cells := make(table.Row, len(m.cfg.Columns))
351			for j, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
352				cells[j] = c.Cell(item)
353			}
354			rows[i] = cells
355		}
356		m.table.SetRows(rows)
357	
358		// bubbles/table leaves the cursor where it was, so a list that just got
359		// shorter strands it past the end until the user presses a key. It also
360		// reports -1 while there are no rows at all, and that has to be taken back
361		// when rows return — a filter typed past its last match and then corrected
362		// would otherwise leave the table showing rows none of which is selected.
363		switch cursor := m.table.Cursor(); {
364		case len(rows) == 0:
365			// -1 is bubbles' own "nothing selected", and what it reports for a
366			// table that never had rows. Leaving the old index would make an empty
367			// list the one state where the cursor points past the end.
368			m.table.SetCursor(-1)
369		case cursor >= len(rows):
370			m.table.SetCursor(len(rows) - 1)
371		case cursor < 0:
372			m.table.SetCursor(0)
373		}
374		m.applyStyles()
375	}
376	
377	// applyStyles asks the view for the styles that go with the selected item.
378	func (m *Model[T]) applyStyles() {
379		if !m.table.Focused() {
380			return // Blur owns the styles until Focus takes them back
381		}
382		styles := theme.DefaultTableStyles()
383		if item, ok := m.Selected(); ok && m.cfg.SelectedStyles != nil {
384			styles = m.cfg.SelectedStyles(item)
385		}
386		// Pin the selected row to the full content width. Column widths are counted
387		// in cells, and a Nerd Font icon does not always render as wide as it
388		// counts, so the highlight otherwise stops short of the right border by
389		// however much the row's icons disagreed. Padding to a width the row can
390		// never exceed is a no-op when they agree.
391		if m.width > 2 {
392			styles.Selected = styles.Selected.Width(m.width - 2)
393		}
394		m.table.SetStyles(styles)
395	}
396	
397	// filtered applies the search query and the toggle filters.
398	func (m *Model[T]) filtered() []T {
399		query := strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(m.bar.SearchQuery()))
400		active := m.activeTokens()
401	
402		out := make([]T, 0, len(m.items))
403		for _, item := range m.items {
404			if m.cfg.TokenMatch != nil && !m.cfg.TokenMatch(item, active) {
405				continue
406			}
407			if query != "" && !m.matchesQuery(item, query) {
408				continue
409			}
410			out = append(out, item)
411		}
412		return out
413	}
414	
415	func (m *Model[T]) activeTokens() map[string]bool {
416		active := make(map[string]bool, len(m.cfg.Tokens))
417		for _, tok := range m.cfg.Tokens {
418			if m.bar.IsTokenActive(tok.Label) {
419				active[tok.Label] = true
420			}
421		}
422		return active
423	}
424	
425	// matchesQuery tests the query against each searchable column and then against
426	// the row as a whole.
427	//
428	// The row-level pass is what keeps a query spanning two fields — "tcp 22" over a
429	// ports list — working: netdiag matched against a joined haystack while the
430	// other four filter loops matched per field, and per field alone would have
431	// quietly dropped those matches on migration. Matching both ways is a superset
432	// of either, so no view loses anything and they all gain the same thing.
433	func (m *Model[T]) matchesQuery(item T, query string) bool {
434		var joined strings.Builder
435		for _, c := range m.cfg.Columns {
436			if c.Search == nil {
437				continue
438			}
439			value := c.Search(item)
440			if strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(value), query) {
441				return true
442			}
443			if joined.Len() > 0 {
444				joined.WriteByte(' ')
445			}
446			joined.WriteString(value)
447		}
448		return strings.Contains(strings.ToLower(joined.String()), query)
449	}
450	
451	// sorted orders the visible slice. SliceStable, because sort.Slice is not and
452	// two rows equal on the sort column would otherwise swap between rebuilds.
453	func (m *Model[T]) sorted(items []T) []T {
454		if m.sortColumn < 0 {
455			return items
456		}
457		less := m.cfg.Columns[m.sortColumn].Less // never nil — see New
458		desc := m.sortDesc
459		sort.SliceStable(items, func(i, j int) bool {
460			if desc {
461				return less(items[j], items[i])
462			}
463			return less(items[i], items[j])
464		})
465		return items
466	}

21	//

23	// into the model for any of that. Carrying it on the row instead is what keeps
24	// the sort honest: the C column orders by the same number it prints, where the
25	// old comparator looked the entry up a second time.
26	type imageRow struct {
27		Image        docker.Image
28		DisplayName  string
29		RawName      string
30		Entry        cache.ImageScanEntry
31		Scanned      bool
32		Scanning     bool
33		Failed       bool

35	}

41	func cveColumn(title string, get func(cache.ImageScanEntry) int) datatable.Column[imageRow] {
42		return datatable.Column[imageRow]{
43			Title: title, MinWidth: 4,
44			Cell: func(r imageRow) string { return formatCVECount(get(r.Entry), r.Scanned) },
45			Less: func(a, b imageRow) bool { return get(a.Entry) < get(b.Entry) },
46		}
47	}

50	// when the last attempt failed, otherwise how long ago it succeeded.

52		switch {
53		case r.Scanning:
54			return r.SpinnerFrame + "scanning"
55		case r.Failed:
56			return theme.IconError + " error"

1	// Package testutil provides helpers for driving Bubble Tea models in tests.
2	//
3	// The views in this project are testable without a terminal because of two
4	// properties the codebase already guarantees:
5	//
6	//   - Constructors are pure. New(cfg) performs no I/O; Docker and network calls
7	//     are issued from Init() as tea.Cmd values.
8	//   - Update() is a pure function (Model, Msg) -> (Model, Cmd). Rule 110 forbids
9	//     mutating the model inside a Cmd, so feeding synthetic messages to Update()
10	//     fully determines the resulting state.
11	//
12	// These helpers therefore build messages and drain commands; they never spin up
13	// a tea.Program.
14	package testutil
15	
16	import (
17		"reflect"
18		"strings"
19	
20		tea "github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea"
21	)
22	
23	// namedKeys maps the key names used throughout the views (they all dispatch on
24	// tea.KeyMsg.String()) onto the key types that render back to those names.
25	var namedKeys = map[string]tea.KeyType{
26		"enter":     tea.KeyEnter,
27		"esc":       tea.KeyEsc,
28		"escape":    tea.KeyEscape,
29		"up":        tea.KeyUp,
30		"down":      tea.KeyDown,
31		"left":      tea.KeyLeft,
32		"right":     tea.KeyRight,
33		"tab":       tea.KeyTab,
34		"shift+tab": tea.KeyShiftTab,
35		" ":         tea.KeySpace,
36		"space":     tea.KeySpace,
37		"backspace": tea.KeyBackspace,
38		"delete":    tea.KeyDelete,
39		"home":      tea.KeyHome,
40		"end":       tea.KeyEnd,
41		"pgup":      tea.KeyPgUp,
42		"pgdown":    tea.KeyPgDown,
43		"ctrl+a":    tea.KeyCtrlA,
44		"ctrl+c":    tea.KeyCtrlC,
45		"ctrl+d":    tea.KeyCtrlD,
46		"ctrl+k":    tea.KeyCtrlK,
47		"ctrl+n":    tea.KeyCtrlN,
48		"ctrl+o":    tea.KeyCtrlO,
49		"ctrl+r":    tea.KeyCtrlR,
50		"ctrl+s":    tea.KeyCtrlS,
51		"ctrl+w":    tea.KeyCtrlW,
52	}
53	
54	// Key builds the tea.KeyMsg whose String() equals name.
55	//
56	// Names listed in namedKeys map to their dedicated key type ("enter", "esc",
57	// "ctrl+s", " "). An "alt+" prefix sets the Alt modifier on whatever follows,
58	// which is how bubbletea reports the ESC-prefixed sequence a terminal sends for
59	// Alt — Key("alt+:") is a colon carrying Alt, not the five runes "alt+:".
60	// Anything else is treated as literal runes, so Key("y") and Key("gg") produce
61	// the rune messages a view matching on those strings expects.
62	func Key(name string) tea.KeyMsg {
63		if rest, isAlt := strings.CutPrefix(name, "alt+"); isAlt && rest != "" {
64			msg := Key(rest)
65			msg.Alt = true
66			return msg
67		}
68		if kt, ok := namedKeys[name]; ok {
69			return tea.KeyMsg{Type: kt}
70		}
71		return tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune(name)}
72	}
73	
74	// Keys builds one message per name, for feeding a sequence to Update().
75	func Keys(names ...string) []tea.Msg {
76		msgs := make([]tea.Msg, 0, len(names))
77		for _, n := range names {
78			msgs = append(msgs, Key(n))
79		}
80		return msgs
81	}
82	
83	// Type builds one rune message per character of s, reproducing a user typing
84	// into a text input. Use this instead of Key(s) when the target is a
85	// bubbles/textinput: it consumes runes one keypress at a time.
86	func Type(s string) []tea.Msg {
87		msgs := make([]tea.Msg, 0, len(s))
88		for _, r := range s {
89			msgs = append(msgs, tea.KeyMsg{Type: tea.KeyRunes, Runes: []rune{r}})
90		}
91		return msgs
92	}
93	
94	// Resize builds the window size message views use to lay themselves out.
95	func Resize(width, height int) tea.Msg {
96		return tea.WindowSizeMsg{Width: width, Height: height}
97	}
98	
99	// Msgs executes cmd and returns every message it produced, flattening the
100	// tea.Batch and tea.Sequence trees. A nil command, or one returning nil, yields
101	// no messages.
102	//
103	// The command runs synchronously on the calling goroutine. Do not pass a command
104	// that sleeps or performs I/O — tea.Tick blocks for its whole duration, and the
105	// Docker runners shell out. Assert on the command's identity or on model state
106	// instead for those.
107	func Msgs(cmd tea.Cmd) []tea.Msg {
108		if cmd == nil {
109			return nil
110		}
111		msg := cmd()
112		if msg == nil {
113			return nil
114		}
115		if batch, ok := msg.(tea.BatchMsg); ok {
116			var out []tea.Msg
117			for _, c := range batch {
118				out = append(out, Msgs(c)...)
119			}
120			return out
121		}
122		if seq, ok := sequenced(msg); ok {
123			var out []tea.Msg
124			for _, c := range seq {
125				out = append(out, Msgs(c)...)
126			}
127			return out
128		}
129		return []tea.Msg{msg}
130	}
131	
132	// sequenced reports whether msg is what tea.Sequence returns, and unpacks the
133	// commands it holds.
134	//
135	// tea.Batch answers with the exported tea.BatchMsg, but the equivalent for
136	// tea.Sequence is unexported — the runtime is its only intended reader, and it
137	// runs the commands one after another rather than concurrently. Its underlying
138	// type is []tea.Cmd, so reflection recovers them without depending on the name.
139	// Order is preserved, which is the whole point of a sequence: a view that emits
140	// "scan starting" before the scan itself relies on the first message arriving
141	// first.
142	func sequenced(msg tea.Msg) ([]tea.Cmd, bool) {
143		value := reflect.ValueOf(msg)
144		if value.Kind() != reflect.Slice || value.Type().Elem() != reflect.TypeFor[tea.Cmd]() {
145			return nil, false
146		}
147		// The element type was just checked, so every assertion below holds; a nil
148		// entry comes back as a nil tea.Cmd, which Msgs already ignores.
149		cmds := make([]tea.Cmd, 0, value.Len())
150		for i := range value.Len() {
151			cmds = append(cmds, value.Index(i).Interface().(tea.Cmd))
152		}
153		return cmds, true
154	}
155	
156	// Msg executes cmd and returns the single message it produced, or nil.
157	// It is the common case of Msgs for commands that emit exactly one message.
158	func Msg(cmd tea.Cmd) tea.Msg {
159		msgs := Msgs(cmd)
160		if len(msgs) == 0 {
161			return nil
162		}
163		return msgs[0]
164	}
165	
166	// MsgOf reports whether cmd produced a message of type T, returning the first
167	// such message. It searches through batched commands.
168	func MsgOf[T tea.Msg](cmd tea.Cmd) (T, bool) {
169		for _, m := range Msgs(cmd) {
170			if v, ok := m.(T); ok {
171				return v, true
172			}
173		}
174		var zero T
175		return zero, false
176	}
177

Date:   Wed Aug 5 14:39:02 2026 +0200

    feat: a configuration view (phase 1) (#43)
    
    * feat: a configuration view (phase 1)
    
    Every scalar setting a context carries -- twenty-nine of them across five
    tabs -- was previously editable only by hand-editing YAML. secret_backend
    is the case that settles it: a documented security decision with three
    values and a fallback, and no way to change it from the application.
    
    Lists stay where they are consulted. Monitors keep their CRUD in status,
    registries keep RegistryForm in oci-resources; duplicating them here would
    be the opposite of the point.
    
    Tabs are not decoration. Rule 135 reserves Tab for tabs and up/down for
    fields, so a tabbed form is the only layout where both keys have exactly
    one job.
    
    Settings are a table of `field` values, each holding one pointer accessor
    into the config rather than a get/set pair. Twenty-nine settings with two
    closures each is where the copy-paste defects of section 2 came from; one
    reference means the read and the write cannot disagree about which setting
    they mean. Two table-level tests keep it honest: every field carries the
    accessor its kind needs, and no two fields address the same setting.
    
    A refused value keeps the cursor on its field. An unparseable integer or a
    malformed Trivy address is reported and not written -- coercing to zero is
    how trivy_server: ":" reached a config file.
    
    Two settings are special-cased. The theme applies as it is cycled, or the
    user chooses blind. The secret backend is confirmed when focus leaves the
    field, not on every arrow, and nothing is migrated between backends:
    section 3.9 removed the option that wrote a token to two stores at once,
    and copying one here would rebuild it.
    
    ConfigSavedMsg drops every view except this one, so a save does not throw
    away the cursor after every keystroke. BackendChanged is separate because
    it is the one change no view can rebuild itself into.
    
    Also fixed: "dark" named a theme no picker could show. LoadTheme accepted
    "", "dark" and "default" alike but ListThemes only offered "default", so
    the default config named a theme absent from every list. Found by the new
    field table's own test, normalised in applyDefaults.
    
    golangci-lint 0 issues, full suite green, internal/ui/configuration 81.5%.
    
    Entire-Checkpoint: 78907419ec72
    
    * feat: group the configuration fields and give the view a header
    
    Three things the first pass got wrong, all visible the moment the view is
    actually looked at.
    
    No header: the view never implemented GetTitle(), so the viewport border
    rendered an empty title. It now carries the context -- editing
    workspaces_dir in the wrong context is otherwise silent, since the fields
    look identical in all of them.

# DevDesk Backlog

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-04

Open work for DevDesk: known defects, technical debt, and planned features.
Replaces the former `todo.md` at the repository root. Items completed there
(network topology visualisation, inter-container ping/curl) have been dropped
rather than carried over.

---

## 1. Known defects

**Four open.** Three are in the registry browser and were found while reviewing
the design for §3.8 rather than by a test; the fourth is dead code found by the
phase 6 coverage pass. See [§1.3](#13-open). D1–D11, D15–D20 and D22 are fixed;
§1.1 records what each was and why the chosen fix was the right one.

The five that stayed open longest — D4, D8, D9, D10 and D11 — were parked not
because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

| Network Diag | `internal/ui/netdiag/` | Diagnostics (ping, DNS, traceroute) + real-time port monitor |

===2530-2565===
6. Optional and last: Presidio as a fail-closed second net over the assembled
   payload, behind a config flag. Two containers and a spaCy model is heavy
   for a few kilobytes of already-structured text, and step 2 is what actually
   provides the guarantee.

Later, and explicitly not now: capture as an additional input (bounded by `-c`
and `-G`, `-s 96` by default so payloads cannot be captured at all), and the
deterministic flow summariser that would have to precede it — a pcap does not
fit in a context window, and once the summariser exists it answers most of the
question without a model. `nicolaka/netshoot` (`config.go:218`) already ships
`tcpdump` and `tshark`, and the privileged host-namespace runner exists
(`ports.go:36`, `topology.go:47`), so the missing piece is the analysis, not the
plumbing.

Adjacent candidates, ranked, none settled: Trivy remediation (§3.2 — low
sensitivity, but any suggested base-image bump must be verified by a re-scan,
never trusted); Gitleaks triage (highest value since false positives dominate,
highest risk since the payload *is* the secret — possibly viable by sending rule
name, path and entropy with the match withheld); container log explanation
(logs carry env vars and DSNs routinely).

input.new_string:
### 3.11 `security` becomes an inventory — **phase 2 done**

Phase 2 of [`configuration-view-plan.md`](../.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md).
Phases 0, 0b and 0c shipped as D26, the per-context scan caches and D27; phase 1
shipped the configuration view. This is the landing page that replaces the form,
and phase 3 is what deletes the form.

`:sec` opened on a form asking what to scan and with which options. Every one of
those options now comes from the configuration view (§1.1, D26), and what gets
scanned is either an image the registry knows or something under
`workspaces_dir` — so the form was asking two questions that had already been
answered elsewhere. It now opens on **everything this context has scanned**,
read from the two scan caches: one `datatable` over images and repositories,
sorted by CRITICAL descending, `theme.TimeAgo` for the age (Rule 127).

`enter` opens a row's stored findings, `ctrl+s` rescans one, `ctrl+a` purges and
rescans all (Rule 126), `ctrl+r` reloads from the caches.

Four things settled while building it:

- **The inventory runs its own scans.** With the options in the config there is
  nothing left to carry to whoever would run one, which is the whole reason the
  cross-view delegation existed. It writes to the same two caches, so a rescan
  here and a `ctrl+s` in the images list are the same operation.
- **`ctrl+a` purges the counts, not the rows.** The rows *are* the list of what
  has been scanned; dropping them would empty the view for the length of the
  scans and lose the targets entirely on a close. A purged row prints `-`, not
  `0` — nothing found and nothing known are different answers, and zero is the
  one that reads as clean.
- **A reload keeps an in-flight scan's marker.** The cache says nothing about a
  scan that has not finished writing to it, so a refresh landing mid-rescan
  would clear the spinner and leave the row looking settled.
- **A finished rescan is routed to the security view wherever the user is**
  (`routeToSecurityView`), for the reason `routeToOCIImagesView` already exists:
  the router forwards everything else to the active view only, and a lost
  completion leaves a row spinning for the life of the view.

`homeState` records where `esc` and `ctrl+r` return to from the results — the
inventory for a view opened on `:sec`, the form for one opened with a target
prefilled. A scan that *fails* uses it too: one started from the inventory must
not land the user on a form they never opened. The field disappears in phase 3,
when there is only one answer left.

`datatable.Config` gained `SortDesc`. Ascending is the useless end of a count
column, and cycling `.` past it on every open is not a default. A direction with
no sortable column to apply it to is dropped along with the column, or the first
`.` would open on descending with the arrow on nothing.

Not touched, and deliberately: `OriginView` (it carries navigation, not options
— and gains a third origin), the dependency banner (the dashboard already shows
`shared.State.Tools`), and the form itself, which stays reachable through
`NewWithTarget` and `NewWithImageTarget` until phase 3.

Coverage: `internal/ui/security` 85.6 % → 85.8 %, project total 81.3 % → 81.4 %.

**Security view** (`internal/ui/security/model.go`) has five states:
`StateInventory` (the landing page), `StateInput` (the form, until phase 3),
`StateScanning`, `StateResults` and `StateDetails` (with remediation info).

### The security inventory

`:sec` opens on **everything the current context has scanned**, read from
`ImageScanCache` and `WorkspaceScanCache` — one `datatable` over images and
repositories, sorted by CRITICAL descending. The form it replaced asked two
questions already answered elsewhere: the options come from the configuration
view, and a target is either a known image or something under `workspaces_dir`.

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `enter` | open the row's stored findings (Rule 126: reads the cache, never scans) |
| `ctrl+s` | rescan the row, **overwriting** its entry |
| `ctrl+a` | **purge** every entry and rescan every target |
| `ctrl+r` | reload from the caches |

**The inventory runs its own scans.** With the options in the config there is
nothing to carry to whoever would run one — which is the only reason the
cross-view delegation exists. It writes to the same two caches, so a rescan here
and `ctrl+s` in the images list are the same operation.

Three invariants, each with a test that fails without it:

- **`ctrl+a` purges the counts, not the rows.** The rows *are* the list of what
  has been scanned; dropping them empties the view for the length of the scans
  and loses the targets on a close. A purged row prints `-`, not `0`.
- **A reload keeps an in-flight scan's marker.** The cache says nothing about a
  scan still running, so a refresh landing mid-rescan would clear the spinner
  and leave the row looking settled.
- **`InventoryScanFinishedMsg` is routed to the security view wherever the user
  is** (`app.routeToSecurityView`), the same reason `routeToOCIImagesView`
  exists. Everything else is forwarded to the active view only, and a lost
  completion leaves a row spinning for the life of the view.

`homeState` records where `esc` and `ctrl+r` return to from the results — the
inventory for a view opened on `:sec`, the form for one opened with a target
prefilled (`NewWithTarget`, `NewWithImageTarget`). A **failed** scan uses it
too: one started from the inventory must not land on a form the user never
opened. The field goes with the form in phase 3.

# DevDesk Architecture Codemap

**Last Updated:** 2026-08-01
**File Count:** 105 Go files (~33k LOC)
**Entry Points:** `main.go` → `internal/app/app.go` (router)

## System Overview

DevDesk is a **Bubble Tea TUI application** implementing multi-view navigation with shared state. The architecture follows the Elm pattern: `Update()` modifies state, `View()` renders, `Cmd` functions perform I/O and return messages.

```
main.go
  ↓
config.Load() → theme.ApplyTheme()
  ↓
app.New() → Router (currentView, views map, sharedState)
  ↓
Bubble Tea program.Run()
```

## View Routing Architecture

**App Router** (`internal/app/app.go`) orchestrates view switching and command mode:

| Component | Purpose |
|-----------|---------|
| `App.currentView` | Active view type (ViewType enum) |
| `App.views` | Lazy-loaded view instances (map[ViewType]tea.Model) |
| `App.sharedState` | Cross-view data (GitLab client, cache, stats) |
| `App.commandMode` | Command input (`:/` prefix) active state |
| `App.commandInput` | textinput.Model for `:cmd` mode |

**View Command Map** (`internal/command/parser.go`):

```
:d[ashboard]      → ViewDashboard
:s[tatus]         → ViewStatus
:gla[uth]         → ViewGitlabAuth
:gle[xplorer]     → ViewGitlabExplorer
:w[orkspaces]     → ViewWorkspaces
:sec[urity]       → ViewSecurity
:cont[ainers]     → ViewContainers
:oci[-resources]  → ViewOCIResources
:net[diag]        → ViewNet
:ctx[context]     → Context switch (reinit views)
:quit / :q        → Exit app
```

## View Models

| View | File | Purpose |
|------|------|---------|
| Dashboard | `internal/ui/dashboard/` | Stats aggregator, tool availability, service health |
| Status | `internal/ui/status/` | HTTP/HTTPS/ICMP/DNS monitors, CRUD operations |
| GitLab Auth | `internal/ui/gitlab/auth/` | Token entry, authentication state |
| GitLab Explorer | `internal/ui/gitlab/explorer/` | Group/project browser, clone/pull, creation |
| Workspaces | `internal/ui/workspaces/` | Local git repos, CRUD, terminal launch, selection mode |
| Security | `internal/ui/security/` | Trivy + Gitleaks scanning, result tabs |
| Containers | `internal/ui/containers/` | Docker container list, metrics, control |
| OCI Resources | `internal/ui/oci_resources/` | Registry images, scan, launch, network inspect |
| Network Diag | `internal/ui/netdiag/` | Diagnostics (ping, DNS, traceroute) + real-time port monitor |

## Data Flow

### Shared State (`internal/shared/state.go`)

Injected at view creation, holds mutable cross-view data:

```go
type State struct {
  GitLabClient    *gitlabclient.Client
  IsAuthenticated bool
  CurrentUser     *gitlabclient.User
  CachedGroups    []*gitlabclient.Group
  CachedProjects  []*gitlabclient.Project
  ServiceStatus   ServiceGlobalStatus  // all_ok|degraded|down|unknown
  ServiceComponents []status.ComponentStatus
  GitLabStats, DockerStats, OCIStats
  WorkspaceCount  int
  Tools           []ToolInfo
}
```

### Message Flow

**Inter-view messages** (`internal/app/messages.go`):
- `SwitchViewMsg{View}` — navigation
- `GitLabAuthSuccessMsg`, `GitLabLogoutMsg` — auth state
- `PullCompletedMsg`, `PullErrorMsg` — sync feedback
- `WorkspaceScanResultLoadedMsg`, `ImageScanResultLoadedMsg` — cache loading

**Per-view messages** defined in each view's `model.go`:
- `TickMsg`, `CheckCompleteMsg`, `FormSubmitMsg`, etc.

### Command Execution

Commands (I/O operations) return to `Update()`:

```
view.Update(msg) → (tea.Model, tea.Cmd)
                     ↓
                   Cmd func
                     ↓
              tea.Msg (sent back to Update)
```

## UI Layout (`internal/ui/theme/`)

**Fixed header** (7 lines):
- View name + shortcuts (top 2 lines)
- Keybindings (5 lines)

**Viewport** (dynamic):
- Bordered rectangle, content rendered via `lipgloss`
- Background propagation via `theme.Bg*()` helpers

**Footer** (2–3 lines):
- Tab bar (if present)
- Empty line separator
- Info line (status/error centered)

## Package Structure

| Package | Responsibility |
|---------|-----------------|
| `internal/app/` | Router, view switching, command dispatch (1540 LOC) |
| `internal/ui/{views}/` | Individual view models + Update/View |
| `internal/ui/components/` | Reusable: filter bar, modals, wrapped input |
| `internal/ui/theme/` | Colors, styles, icons, time formatting |
| `internal/command/` | Parser, completion engine |
| `internal/config/` | YAML loading, multi-context support |
| `internal/shared/` | Cross-view state struct |
| `internal/cache/` | Image/workspace scan caches (metadata + results) |
| `internal/scan/` | Trivy/Gitleaks orchestrator |
| `internal/docker/` | Docker CLI wrapper, network diag tools |
| `internal/oci/` | OCI registry HTTP client |
| `internal/gitlab/` | GitLab API client wrapper, auth, git ops |
| `internal/status/` | Health checker (HTTP/ICMP/DNS) |
| `internal/credentials/` | Storage interface: File/Memory/GitCredential |

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules (Rule 110)

- **Never modify state in Cmd** — only in `Update()`
- **Never use `style.Render()` in table.Row{}** — causes ANSI corruption
- **View must implement FormView.InEditMode()** if active forms block command mode
- **Footer messages disappear after 3 seconds** via `clearFooterMsgCmd()`

## Context Switching

Context names stored in `~/.devdesk/current-context`. On switch:
1. Load new config from `~/.devdesk/contexts/<name>/config.yaml`
2. Reinitialize all views with new config
3. Update sharedState (GitLab client, etc.)
4. Emit `tea.WindowSizeMsg` to trigger resize

## Initialization Chain

```
main()
  → config.Load() [from ~/.devdesk/config.yaml or current context]
  → theme.LoadTheme() [if config.App.Theme set]
  → app.New(cfg)
     → new(views map)
     → dashboard.New() + status.New()  [eager]
     → other views lazy-loaded on first `:cmd`
     → sharedState initialized
  → tea.NewProgram().Run()
```

Phase 2 of [`configuration-view-plan.md`](.claude/plans/configuration-view-plan.md). This is the landing page that replaces the form — **phase 3 is what deletes the form**, and it stays reachable until then.

## What changes

`:sec` opened on a form asking what to scan and with which options. Every one of those options now comes from the configuration view, and what gets scanned is either an image the registry knows or something under `workspaces_dir` — so the form was asking two questions already answered elsewhere.

It now opens on **everything this context has scanned**, read from the two scan caches: one `datatable` over images and repositories, sorted by CRITICAL descending, `theme.TimeAgo` for the age (Rule 127).

| Key | Effect |
|---|---|
| `enter` | open the row's stored findings (Rule 126: reads the cache, never scans) |
| `ctrl+s` | rescan the row, **overwriting** its entry |
| `ctrl+a` | **purge** every entry and rescan every target |
| `ctrl+r` | reload from the caches |
| `/` `.` | filter, cycle sort |

**The inventory runs its own scans.** With the options in the config there is nothing left to carry to whoever would run one, which is the whole reason the cross-view delegation exists. It writes to the same two caches, so a rescan here and `ctrl+s` in the images list are the same operation.

## Three invariants, each confirmed to bite by removing it

- **`ctrl+a` purges the counts, not the rows.** The rows *are* the list of what has been scanned; dropping them empties the view for the length of the scans and loses the targets on a close. A purged row prints `-`, not `0` — nothing found and nothing known are different answers, and zero is the one that reads as clean.
- **A reload keeps an in-flight scan's marker.** The cache says nothing about a scan that has not finished writing to it, so a refresh landing mid-rescan would clear the spinner and leave the row looking settled.
- **`InventoryScanFinishedMsg` is routed to the security view wherever the user is** (`routeToSecurityView`), for the reason `routeToOCIImagesView` already exists: the router forwards everything else to the active view only, and a lost completion leaves a row spinning for the life of the view.

`homeState` records where `esc` and `ctrl+r` return to from the results — the inventory for a view opened on `:sec`, the form for one opened with a target prefilled. A scan that *fails* uses it too: one started from the inventory must not land the user on a form they never opened. The field goes with the form in phase 3.

`datatable.Config` gained `SortDesc`. Ascending is the useless end of a count column, and cycling `.` past it on every open is not a default. A direction with no sortable column to apply it to is dropped along with the column, or the first `.` would open descending with the arrow on nothing.

`OriginView` (it carries navigation, not options — and gains a third origin), the dependency banner (the dashboard already shows `shared.State.Tools`), and the form itself.

content.text:
Phase 2 of the configuration-view plan is done and up as **[PR #44](https://github.com/anthnel/devdesk/pull/44)**.

## What shipped

`:sec` now opens on an **inventory** of everything the current context has scanned — one `datatable` over both scan caches (images and repositories), sorted by CRITICAL descending. `enter` opens a row's stored findings, `ctrl+s` rescans one, `ctrl+a` purges and rescans all, `ctrl+r` reloads.

The inventory runs its own scans rather than delegating back to the originating view: with the options now in the config, there is nothing left to carry across.

## Three things the plan didn't anticipate

- **`ctrl+a` purges the counts, not the rows.** Here the rows *are* the cache, unlike the images tab where they come from Docker — purging them would empty the view for the length of the scans and lose the targets on a close. A purged row prints `-`, not `0`.
- **A reload has to keep an in-flight scan's marker**, or a refresh landing mid-rescan clears the spinner and the row looks settled while its scan is still running.
- **`InventoryScanFinishedMsg` needs routing to the security view wherever the user is.** The router forwards everything else to the active view only, so leaving the view mid-rescan would have left a row spinning for the life of the view. `routeToOCIImagesView` already existed for exactly this.

I also added `SortDesc` to `datatable.Config` — the plan asks for CRITICAL-descending on open and the component could only express ascending.

## Verification

`go build`, `go vet`, `golangci-lint` (0 issues) and the full suite are green. Coverage went **up**: `internal/ui/security` 85.6% → 85.9%, project total 81.3% → 81.4% (measured against `main` by stashing). I confirmed each new invariant bites by removing its implementation and watching the specific test fail — purge, reload marker, spinner chain, esc-reload, routing, and both `SortDesc` cases.

## Two things to note

The form is **not** deleted — that is phase 3, and it stays reachable through `NewWithTarget`/`NewWithImageTarget`. Its tests still pass and still describe it; I made `newTestModel` ask for `StateInput` explicitly rather than assume it.

I have not run the TUI itself — the test plan in the PR leaves three manual checks unticked (the rows on a real context, leaving mid-rescan, and the empty state). Everything asserted above is from the automated suite.

content.text:
Analyse faite. Voici les faits.

## Ce que le header affiche aujourd'hui

`GetHeaderInfo` (`internal/ui/security/header.go:118`) ne dépend que de `m.deps` et de `m.result` — pas de l'état :

| État | Colonne info |
|---|---|
| Inventory | Trivy, Gitleaks |
| Input (form) | Trivy, Gitleaks |
| Scanning | Trivy, Gitleaks |
| Results / Details | Trivy, Gitleaks, Duration, Filter, Secrets, Licenses, CVEs — **7** |

## 1. Le contexte est absent, et c'est ma faute

La signature est `GetHeaderInfo(_ string)` : **le paramètre `context` est jeté**. Le routeur le passe pourtant (`app_header.go:46`), et `workspaces` s'en sert exactement comme il faut (`view.go:408` → `{Key: "Context", Value: context}`).

J'ai mis le contexte dans `GetTitle()` en phase 2. C'était le mauvais endroit : la convention du projet le met dans la colonne info, et l'inventaire est précisément la vue où il compte le plus — les caches sont scopés par contexte, donc deux contextes affichent des lignes d'apparence identique tirées de données différentes.

## 2. La contrainte dure que personne ne voit

`buildInfoLines` (`app_header.go:112`) construit **exactement 7 lignes** et ne lit jamais `info[7]` et au-delà — sans erreur, sans log. L'état Results est **déjà à 7**. Ajouter « Context » aujourd'hui ferait disparaître la barre CVE silencieusement. Le ménage n'est donc pas cosmétique : il est ce qui rend la place disponible.

## 3. Les champs qui n'ont plus lieu d'être

- **Trivy / Gitleaks sur l'inventaire** — le plan l'avait déjà tranché : « the dependency banner does not move… the dashboard already carries `shared.State.Tools` and shows exactly this ». Ces deux champs répondent à « puis-je scanner ? », l'inventaire répond à « qu'ai-je scanné ? ». Sur le formulaire ils gardent leur sens (ils expliquent le bouton grisé) — jusqu'à la phase 3.
- **Filter** — affiche `ALL` en permanence, et n'a aucun sens sur l'onglet Secrets (où `.` ne filtre pas) ni en Details (où `.` ne fait rien). C'est de l'état transitoire, qui relève du footer (Rule 128).
- **Secrets / Licenses** — duplication franche de la barre d'onglets, qui rend déjà `Secrets (n)` et `Licenses (n)` (`view.go:337`). Pire : les deux nombres viennent de **deux classificateurs différents** — `result.SecretCount` (`scan/scanner.go:126`, switch sur `Source`) contre `countFindingsByTab` (`findings.go:151`, switch sur `Source` + `PkgName` + `Match`). C'est la famille D24/D25/D26.

Ce qui **mérite** de rester : **CVEs** (la barre de sévérité n'apparaît nulle part ailleurs) et **Duration**.

## 4. Ce qui manque

Sur l'inventaire, l'équivalent de ce que fait `oci_resources` (`Images: n` + volumétrie) : nombre de cibles et total des findings. Sur les résultats, quand le scan a eu lieu — un résultat sorti du cache affiche une `Duration` de plusieurs jours sans rien qui le dise.

## Proposition

| État | Info proposée |
|---|---|
| Inventory | Context, Targets (`n images · m repos`), CRIT total, Scanned (le plus récent) |
| Input / Scanning | Context, Trivy, Gitleaks |
| Results / Details | Context, Target, Scanned, Duration, CVEs |

Soit 5 champs max partout — deux de marge sous le plafond de 7. `Filter`, `Secrets` et `Licenses` disparaissent ; le filtre de sévérité est déjà visible via le raccourci `.` et pourrait aller en footer si tu y tiens.

## Deux choses trouvées au passage, hors périmètre

**Les deux classificateurs divergent réellement.** Vérifié par sonde puis supprimée :

| Finding | `scan.CountFindings` | onglets de la vue |
|---|---|---|
| `trivy`, `PkgName` vide | CVE = 1 | **aucun onglet** |
| source inconnue | CVE = 1 | **aucun onglet** |
| `trivy` + `Match` | CVE = 1 | Secrets = 1 |

Aujourd'hui les totaux affichés coïncident quand même, parce qu'aucun de ces trois cas n'est produit — mais un finding compté dans la barre CVE et absent de toute table est invisible dans l'interface. C'est latent, pas actif : je ne peux pas confirmer que Trivy émette un `PkgName` vide.

**`TrivyResult.Secrets` est parsé et jamais lu.** Le champ existe (`scan/trivy.go:22`), le type `TrivySecret` aussi (`:41`), et rien ne le parcourt — `trivy.go` ne construit des `Finding` que depuis `Vulnerabilities`, `Licenses` et `Misconfigurations`. L'aide de la vue annonce pourtant « Secret Scan: … (Gitleaks + Trivy) ». Même forme que D27 : déclaré, défaut, jamais lu. C'est aussi ce qui rend la branche `Source == "trivy" && Match != ""` inatteignable.

---

Je n'ai rien modifié — tu as demandé une analyse, et la PR #44 est inchangée. Dis-moi si j'applique la proposition (ce serait un commit sur la même branche), et si les deux points hors périmètre vont dans `docs/backlog.md` §1.3 comme défauts ouverts.
